open_items: The screener reads M-1 from Union City's zoning layer on ArcGIS Online, which no polite fetch can reach (robots.txt answers 403); Union City's own site answers 403 and its code is on Municode (a known wall). Not verified here: a person should confirm the district, any conditions attached at a past rezoning, and whether warehouse/distribution is permitted by right in M-1.

A search-result snippet (not verified, a listing site) described the owner's neighbouring distribution centre as zoned M1C, i.e. possibly a conditional M-1. Ask Union City planning whether this parcel was part of the same conditional zoning and what conditions bind it.

The county tax roll gives this parcel class R5 and land-use code 100 (see the market claim's quote), not an industrial class; the tax class does not decide zoning, but a person should ask why it is classed that way.

claims.text: Union City's 2020 comprehensive plan (as submitted to ARC, January 2021) applies its District-Industrial character area near US-29, South Fulton Parkway and rail lines; this parcel fronts SR 14 / US-29 (Roosevelt Hwy) beside the CSX line and adjoins the owner's distribution centre on South Fulton Parkway. That the parcel itself sits inside the D-I area on the Future Development Map (pdf page 78) is the investigator's reading of a low-resolution map image, not a verified fact.

open_items: Confirm on Union City's current Future Development Map (and any update after 2020) which character area covers this parcel; the map in the ARC copy is too coarse to place a 13-acre parcel with certainty.

Rezoning history of the last five years not checked: Union City's agendas and minutes are on its own site, which answers 403. Ask the city for any rezoning, variance or site-plan case on this parcel and the owner's neighbouring parcels since 2021.

No ARC DRI was found for this parcel in ten web searches; nearby DRIs (Union City Commerce Center 2021, Airport Distribution Center Four 2022, ATL11 2024) are on other sites (Evans Drive and Stonewall Tell Road).

claims.text: Sewer: Fulton County's Waste Water Pipe layer (WaterResourcesSewer MapServer layer 4), asked for pipes intersecting this parcel's outline (the county parcel polygon simplified to 5 ft, state plane), returns six active 8-inch gravity segments, Fulton County service area, Camp Creek basin, i.e. a public sewer line runs across the parcel.

Water: Fulton County's Water Pipe layer (same service, layer 18), asked for pipes within 1,000 ft of this parcel's outline, returns no feature. Fulton County may not be the water provider in Union City (its service-area layers 19 and 22 also returned nothing here), so this is not evidence of no water; the provider's own map was not found.

open_items: Identify the water provider for this part of Union City and ask for the nearest main and its size; the owner's distribution centre on the adjoining parcel is presumably served, but that was not checked.
Sewer capacity and whether the 8-inch line crossing the parcel sits in an easement that constrains the building pad: only the utility and a title search can say.
The assessor's 'Septic' entry in the brief predates or ignores the mapped sewer line; treat it as unreliable.

claims.text: Asked by parcel id, Fulton County's tax parcel layer (tax year 2027) still lists the operator itself as owner of this parcel, with no improvement value. In the places looked (this record, ARC DRI reviews reached by search, ten web searches by site address and parcel id) no listing, contract, third-party rezoning or development-authority action on this parcel was found. This is not evidence it is for sale; see the owner section.

open_items: Search-result snippets (not verified; news sites, not read) carried headlines that the owner paid about $40M to expand its land holdings near its Atlanta-airport distribution centre, about 33 acres along Roosevelt Highway straddling Union City and South Fulton. If that purchase includes this parcel (the brief's 2021-08-26 sale and the three same-owner neighbours total about 30 acres), the land was bought as expansion land for the operator's own facility and is unlikely to be sold. A person should read those articles.
The county GIS polygon for this parcel measures about 20.8 acres (Shape area 907,300 sq ft) while the roll says 12.94 acres; check the deed and plat before relying on either.

By the investigator's own computation from the county parcel geometry, that parcel shares about 2,050 ft of boundary with this lead: the lead adjoins the owner's operating facility (search results name it the owner's distribution centre; not verified on a primary page).

open_items: Georgia Secretary of State record not read (known wall: 403). On the county roll the owner holds improved industrial parcels next door (claims above); the lead looks like expansion or buffer land for its distribution centre rather than surplus land.

Ask (through the person, not by contact from here) whether the owner has a site plan, permit or expansion plan for this parcel and its three same-owner neighbours; the screen's 'possible assemblage' is most likely the operator's own expansion holding.

skeptic.objection: No document found (site plan, permit, ARC DRI, development-authority item) shows what the owner plans for this parcel, so 'expansion or buffer land, not available' is still an inference. But the inference holds up: the county map confirms the lead touches the owner's improved 94.3-acre operating parcel and one of its vacant same-owner neighbours, and nothing shows it for sale. The lead's acreage is also in doubt: its map shape is 20.83 acres against 12.94 on the roll, while the adjoining parcel's map and roll agree exactly. The screener's building fit and pond allowance rest on the map shape, so the usable area and the 104,000 SF fit are unproven until a deed and plat are read.

claims.text: Acreage: Fulton County's tax parcel layer, asked for the parcels intersecting this lead's outline, gives this parcel (FeatureID 09F350001311327) a roll acreage of 12.94 but a map shape of 907,300.5 sq ft (Georgia West state plane feet), i.e. 20.83 acres: the map shape is about 7.9 acres (61%) larger than the roll. The first pass's 20.8-acre figure is confirmed.

Acreage control: on the same page the adjoining 94.3-acre parcel (FeatureID 09F350001311319) has a map shape of 4,107,725 sq ft, i.e. 94.30 acres, matching its roll acreage exactly. The gap on the lead is specific to this parcel, not a projection or map-wide effect; the screener's building fit (largest open part 14.8 acres, more than the 12.94 roll acres) rests on a map shape the deed may not support.

Adjacency: the county tax parcel layer, asked for parcels intersecting this lead's outline (the same simplified polygon the first pass used in its sewer query), returns the owner's improved 94.3-acre parcel at 4250 South Fulton Pkwy. This supports owner-1's statement that the lead touches the owner's operating site (the length of the shared line is not shown here).

The same intersect query also returns the same-owner 5.49-acre parcel at 5190 Cooks Rd (09F260301261215), so the lead touches the owner's operating parcel and one of its three vacant same-owner neighbours directly; the other two (09F260301260944, 09F260301261181) are not returned and connect only through 5190 Cooks Rd, if at all.

Fulton County's Yearly Sales 2021 layer, asked by parcel id, lists this lead as a 2021 sale record with price 0 (no price shown) and already with the 907,300 sq ft (20.8-acre) map shape. The oversized map shape is not a recent map edit: it was on the county map in the year of the brief's 2021-08-26 sale. The layer does not confirm the brief's $9,097,000 price.

Regional review: the ARC DRI on Roosevelt Highway in Union City that the first pass names (Union City Commerce Center, DRI 3266, 277 acres at the end of Evans Drive) is located at these coordinates, about 1.7 miles south-west of this lead (33.6159, -84.5294). It does not cover this parcel. No DRI covering this parcel or the owner's expansion was found.

open_items: plans-1 and plans-2 quote the generic intent and 'Application' text of the District-Industrial character area; neither quote places this parcel in D-I, and plans-1's own text says the placement is an unverified reading of a coarse map. They do not carry the 'supports' verdict; treat plans as unknown until the Future Development Map is read at parcel scale.

Search-result snippets only (Union City's own site answers 403, so it was not fetched and nothing here is verified): the city appears to have adopted, on 2026-03-24, a 180-day moratorium on accepting, processing and approving rezonings, text amendments and conditional use applications while a comprehensive zoning ordinance rewrite (zoning districts, development standards) is under way. Another result is a 2026 application titled as a Future Development Map update. Ask Union City planning whether the rewrite changes M-1 or the D-I area here, and whether the moratorium is still in force.

Search-result snippets only (news sites, not read): a $40M purchase of 33 acres along Roosevelt Highway straddling Union City and South Fulton, near the owner's distribution centre at 4250 South Fulton Pkwy, from a seller that had assembled it, described as vacant land and truck parking. The search tool dated that story about 1,185 days before today (about August 2023), which would not match the brief's 2021-08-26 sale of this parcel. The tie between this parcel and that purchase is unproven either way. A person should read the articles and the deeds.

By my own reading of the county parcel layer (not quoted above): the four same-owner parcels total 30.06 roll acres but about 35.35 map acres. 5190 Cooks Rd maps at 5.14 ac (roll 5.49), 5220 Cooks Rd at 4.58 ac (roll 5.63), and 0 Roosevelt Hwy Rear at 4.80 ac (roll 6.00). A third-party vacant I5 parcel of 10.16 roll acres that touches the lead maps at 10.10 ac. Only the lead's map shape is much larger than its roll. Pull the deed and plat for all four before relying on any acreage.

No site plan, land-disturbance permit, DRI or Development Authority of Fulton County item was found for this parcel or for an expansion at 4250 South Fulton Pkwy. I ran nine web searches by site address, parcel ids, and DRI and development-authority terms; the ARC DRI search found only other sites (DRI 3266 at Evans Drive; ATL11 and Airport Distribution Center Four on Stonewall Tell Road). This is weak evidence: an expansion of truck parking or a building under the DRI threshold need not reach ARC. Ask Union City and, for the South Fulton side, the City of South Fulton for permits or site plans on the four parcels since 2021.

The 5 ft simplified outline used in the intersect query can touch a neighbour that the true outline does not. The adjacency claims are only as good as that polygon; owner-1's 2,050 ft shared boundary was not re-measured here.

Not tested: whether the lead already serves the owner's operating site (for example a detention pond for the distribution centre, given the brief's 11% ponds and the 8-inch public sewer segments crossing the parcel). If it does, it is not surplus land at all. A drive-by or the permit record would tell.

The Fulton County assessor's public-access host (iaspublicaccess.fultoncountyga.gov) reset the connection on its robots.txt and was not fetched, so the 2021 sale price and deed reference were not read from a primary page.

quotecheck.proves: each kept quote was on the page at its URL when this tool fetched it (see pages); nothing more. Claim text, objections and open_items are the agents' own words, not checked
